comparator.name: Mathematics (Wiskunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026-27 Leiden Study Guide and public product API define 60 EC in each year. Year one contains 54 EC of compulsory mathematics and programming plus 6 EC of open elective space. Year two contains a 48-EC compulsory sequence and 12 EC selected from the published restricted electives; Algebra 2 and Discrete Operations Research are selected as the first two options in official order. Year three contains 12 EC of restricted mathematics study, an 18-EC bachelor project and 30 EC of open elective space. Because Algebra 2 and Discrete Operations Research were already used in year two, Algebraic Curves and Applied & Industrial Mathematics Seminar are the first two non-duplicative year-three options in official order. The choices were fixed independently of UCR fit, and all components account for exactly 180 EC.

exception.reason: Leiden's Mathematics bachelor requires a cumulative proof-based sequence in mathematical structures, two courses each in analysis, linear algebra and algebra, followed by topology, complex function theory, measure theory, differential equations, probability and mathematical statistics, numerical mathematics, restricted advanced mathematics and an 18-EC independent mathematics project. UCR offers a useful but small applied mathematics and computing set. It has no course sequence in proof-based real analysis, abstract algebra, topology, measure theory, complex function theory or geometry and no independent mathematics research project. A 24-course response would therefore replace most of the degree's disciplinary core with computing, data science and adjacent applications.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official 2026-27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC through a 60-EC first year, a 60-EC second year and a 60-EC third year. Restricted choices were instantiated by neutral official order before UCR provision was considered. The resulting route retains 36 EC of genuine open elective space and still contains a continuous 126-EC compulsory or restricted mathematics core plus the 18-EC bachelor project.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide applied calculus, linear algebra, numerical, systems and probability tools. DISARIN212 Logic & Discrete Mathematics adds formal and discrete reasoning, while DISARIN311 Optimization Methods in AI provides an adjacent optimisation application. The workbook contains no sustained proof-based analysis or algebra sequence, topology, measure theory, complex function theory, projective or differential geometry, number theory, stochastic-process sequence or mathematics bachelor project. Programming and data-science courses are useful tools but cannot turn the remaining 15 or more non-PPD slots into a coherent Mathematics degree or reproduce the external proof-to-research progression.
